title: Delivering a more consistent and risk-based approach to AML/CFT across Europe: Rikke-Louise Ørum Petersen speaks at AMLP Forum

paras.text: AMLA Executive Board Member Rikke-Louise Ørum Petersen delivered the opening keynote on the second day of AMLP’s 20th Annual European AML/CTF & Financial Crime Conference in London on 10 November 2026.
In her address, Petersen outlined AMLA’s work towards a more consistent and effective European AML/CFT framework, ahead of the application of the Anti-Money Laundering Regulation in July 2027.

She focused on the development of the Single Rulebook, establishing clearer and more consistent requirements proportionate to the risks identified, and on strengthening the link between customer due diligence and ongoing monitoring, highlighting the role of technology in identifying and responding to changes in risk. She also addressed AMLA’s work with national supervisors to promote supervisory convergence and prepare for direct supervision from 2028.

Petersen emphasised the importance of stakeholder engagement, noting how feedback received through public consultations has informed revisions to draft regulatory standards to support their effective implementation.

Looking ahead, she stressed that AMLA’s role extends beyond the institutions it will directly supervise. By promoting consistent regulatory and supervisory approaches and strengthening cooperation among Financial Intelligence Units, AMLA aims to improve the identification, assessment and mitigation of money laundering and terrorist financing risks across the EU.
She concluded by highlighting the importance of continued cooperation between public authorities and the private sector in implementing the new framework.
